name: Герои, партия 4: шестнадцать героев рулетки циклов III–IV без портрета (c3-41…c3-46, c3-64, c3-65, c4-41…c4-46, c4-64, c4-65). Рецепт принятых портретов — jobs/heroes-batch-03.json: тот же стиль, запреты и три референса стиля из art/style; кадр по пояс, корпус вправо, к врагам, камера чуть снизу; способ «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md): кто он и чего хочет сейчас · характер телом · поза словами в миг действия · пять личных деталей из «кто он» и глав · место. В рамке добавлено: нижний край режет фигуру по поясу, низ плавно уходит в тень без плашки и надписей (в партиях Эхо модель дважды рисовала фигуру в рост и один раз подписала имя). Редкость не рисуем, класс — по оружию или действию, школа — по цвету света. Источники: design/ui/roster.js (who, ch) — главы состава docs/content/герои/; лор городов — docs/lore/свод-лора-текст.txt (Лайтен-Гард: белый камень, красная черепица, арки Паладиума с синим камнем в замке свода, Храмовый холм с синими шпилями, кипарисы наверху; обод — паладиумовое ядро в энериумной оправе). «Пришлую лекарку» из глав и путника в рясе не рисуем. У Клеймёного (зверь) — без ref-04, как у Ветверога. Детали, которых нет в главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no writing on paper, books, maps or stones, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no name plate, no dark band at the bottom, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes.

heroes.frame: Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the belt or the hips; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame, whatever the pose. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression. The lower part of the picture sinks gradually into deeper shadow — no band, no plate, nothing written. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

jobs.subject: Subject: Benno, a man of an ordinary land, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: the eldest son of an ordinary family in an ordinary land — work, hunger, brothers, everyone asleep in a heap by one stove. In the hungry winter, while his father and mother searched for food, he carried his little sister on his back through the snow and did not notice that she never grew heavier; he noticed later. Right now something moves in the blizzard beyond the right edge, and he stands between it and what he carries. Character: steady, simple, stubborn and gentle — an ordinary man who does not step back; his broad face set, his brows lowered against the wind, his grey eyes calm and fixed on the danger. A young man, broad-shouldered, with a short fair beard frosted with snow and a weathered, honest face. Pose, the moment of the stand: the camera is low; he plants himself in the snow, turned toward the right, braced against the storm, his shoulders squared. He has exactly two arms: his near arm raises a heavy shield made from an old door of thick planks bound with iron, toward the right; his far hand grips a long wooden pitchfork held low and ready. Amber-orange light of the Earth school bursts from cracks in the frozen ground below, and snow flies. Details that tell his story: (1) on his back a small bundle wrapped in an old patched sheepskin is tied with rope — light as a feather; (2) a peasant's coat of patched brown wool with a rope for a belt; (3) the cracked, calloused hands of a ploughman; (4) a heel of dark bread is tucked into his coat — he did not eat it; (5) snow crusted thick on his shoulders and hood. Place: a poor village of low houses in the hungry winter at dusk: snowdrifts, a single window glowing with the light of one stove, bare trees, a blizzard. Amber light rises from the frozen earth below; cold blue snow-light all around.

jobs.subject: Subject: Veveya the Midwife, a woman of the great harbor city of the west, a healer of the Water school. Who she is: the midwife at the western cradle beneath Temple Hill, by the stones of the first court; she was taught to meet and to see off with the same hands — it is one door, only from two sides. On the day that was lived twice she delivered the same boy twice, and both times he cried out at the same instant; she told no one. Right now she stretches her hands toward a life at the door. Character: calm, strong and afraid of nothing — a midwife who has seen everything; her face kind and firm, her eyes steady. A woman in her forties with a strong jaw and a few grey strands in her dark hair. Pose, the moment of healing: the camera is low; she stands turned toward the right, leaning forward, reaching out. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is stretched toward the right, the palm open and upturned, and a soft stream of cool blue light of the Water school flows from it toward the one beyond the right edge; her far hand holds a folded linen cloth against her chest. Details that tell her story: (1) her sleeves are rolled up over strong forearms, a white linen apron; (2) a copper basin of clean water glowing blue beside her; (3) a small bundle of herbs and a knife at her belt; (4) a heavy old door of dark wood stands half open behind her, with light on both sides of it; (5) a plain kerchief binds her hair. Place: the chamber of the western cradle at night, carved into the foot of a hill: a great smooth ancient stone shaped like a basin, warm lamps, walls of white stone; far above, through an arch, the blue spires of a temple on the hill. Cool blue light of the Water school rises from the basin below; warm lamplight.

jobs.subject: Subject: Aeris Bowstring, an elf of the great southern forest, a swift archer of the Air school. Who he is: he learned to shoot at the great Tree when the forest was young and the Tree did not yet reach the clouds — you could still shout to its top. The elves are monks with bows, and he was one of the best and knew it without pride; he was taught to shoot not at the beast but into the silence between two heartbeats. For two hundred years he stood on the southern edge of the forest. Right now, in that silence, he looses. Character: serene, precise and utterly calm — a master for whom the whole world stops; his face still, his eyes clear and focused, the faintest line between his brows. An elf with a long, fine face, long pointed ears, long pale hair tied back, grey-green eyes. Pose, the moment between two heartbeats: the camera is low; he stands at the edge of the forest, turned toward the right, the bow at full draw. He has exactly two arms: his near arm holds a tall longbow of pale living wood out toward the right; his far hand draws the string back to his cheek, the arrow aimed at the enemy beyond the right edge. Everything around him hangs still: falling leaves stop in mid-air, and a thin spiral of pale white-green wind of the Air school coils along the arrow. Details that tell his story: (1) the bow is of pale living wood with a few green leaves still growing on it; (2) a quiver of arrows fletched with white feathers; (3) a long grey-green cloak with the hood thrown back; (4) a thin braid with a single wooden bead behind his ear; (5) far behind him the great Tree rises above the young forest, its crown still below the clouds. Place: the southern edge of a young elven forest at dawn: slender young trees, clear light, the vast Tree in the distance. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the roots and moss below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Hilda of the Dead Vein, a dwarf woman, a controller of the Dark school who cripples her foes. Who she is: a prospector who found veins by sound — a living vein rings, empty rock goes dull. Once she found a vein that was silent in a different way, its stone glowing with no colour at all, and they laughed at her; later a stone that glows violet was found there, and everyone stopped laughing at once. Later she learned a darkness that puts out another's power — no fitting thing for a dwarf, and she took it. Right now she casts that darkness on an enemy. Character: dour, stubborn and unafraid of what others do not speak of; her mouth a hard line, her heavy brows lowered, her deep-set eyes cold. A dwarf woman in her middle years, short and enormously broad, with heavy braids of dark hair bound with iron rings and a broad weathered face. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she stands in a mine tunnel, turned toward the right, planted like a rock. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is thrust out toward the right, fingers spread, and a wave of violet-black darkness of the Dark school rolls from her palm toward the enemy beyond the right edge, swallowing its light; her far hand holds a small prospector's hammer raised beside her ear, as if she has just tapped the rock and is listening. Details that tell her story: (1) a prospector's belt with small hammers, chisels and a pouch of rock samples; (2) a dull grey vein in the rock wall behind her with a faint violet gleam deep inside it; (3) her knuckles are callused from tapping stone; (4) a miner's lamp hangs from her belt, turned low; (5) a leather hood pushed back, dust in her braids. Place: a deep dwarven mine tunnel inside the mountain: rough stone, timber props, a vein of dead grey stone. Violet light of the Dark school rises from cracks in the floor below; the small warm glow of her lamp.

jobs.subject: Subject: The Branded, a sentient beast, a warrior of great strength of the Earth school. Who he is: he was brought as a cub from the dangerous lands of the east, where the streams smell wrong, to the cages beneath the great northern arena; the two-legged ones burned a mark into his shoulder to know him by and let him out onto the sand. For twenty seasons he did not lose to a single beast, and he remembers every one he did not finish off. Then a chief of the north came out onto the sand against him — and did not strike him when he fell, and opened his cage himself. Right now he charges across the arena sand. Character: savage, proud and fiercely free — a creature who decides for himself, not the pack; his eyes amber and intelligent, burning with fury and pride. Appearance: a colossal wolf-like beast of the east, bigger than a bear, with a heavy mane of dark grey fur on his neck and chest, a broad scarred muzzle and long fangs. Framing and pose, the moment of the charge: he is a beast, and the half-body frame is close: his head, his mane, his chest and his front legs fill the frame, and the rest of his body is out of the frame. The camera is low and looks up at him. He lunges toward the right, his forepaws slamming into the sand, his jaws open in a roar; a burst of sand and amber-orange light of the Earth school explodes under his paws. Details that tell his story: (1) a brand burned into the fur of his shoulder — a plain round scar, pale and hairless; (2) many old scars across his muzzle and chest — twenty seasons of fights; (3) a broken iron collar with a short length of chain hangs from his neck; (4) one ear is torn; (5) arena sand clings to his fur. Place: the sand of the great arena of the north under torches at night: tall stone walls, the iron gates of the cages, a crowd blurred in the darkness above. Amber light rises from the sand below; torch fire behind.

jobs.subject: Subject: Meret the Guide, a woman of the floating city of mages, a battle mage of the Time school who also cripples her foes. Who she is: Time mages feel charged stone in the rock, and the city of mages let her guide caravans across the middle of the world — whoever hears the green hum knows where it is better not to stop. At the last station a green vein hummed, and near the middle of the world sleep comes on you; she told everyone not to sleep and fell asleep first. When she woke she mapped every station where one must not sleep, and for twenty years no caravan of hers fell asleep again. Right now she slows an enemy to a crawl. Character: sharp, stubborn and self-reproaching — a guide who never again lets anyone sleep; her eyes wide awake and alert, her brows drawn, her mouth set. A lean woman in her thirties with short dark hair, a sun-browned face and dark circles under her eyes. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she stands at a caravan station, turned toward the right. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is thrust out toward the right, fingers spread, and a wide wave of green light of the Time school rolls toward the enemy beyond the right edge; inside it the dust and sand hang frozen in mid-air; her far hand holds a leather map case against her hip. Details that tell her story: (1) the map case is of worn leather, rolled maps sticking out of it with nothing written visible; (2) a dusty travelling coat with many pockets over a mage's robe; (3) a small brass hourglass on a chain at her belt; (4) a lantern tied to a staff across her back; (5) a green crystal vein humming in the rock wall behind her. Place: a desolate caravan station in the barren middle of the world at dusk: a stone wall, a well, pack animals dozing in soft focus. Green light of the Time school rises from the vein and the cracks below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Hjalti the Burning, a man of the northern lands, a warrior of great strength of the Fire school. Who he is: a berserker of the north with a scarlet fire stone in his blade. The stone gives nothing and takes nothing — it kindles what is already in a man, and in him there was a fire that only wanted a chance. In battle the stone took away his fear, his pain and his weariness, and he went first and laughed, because there was nothing to feel. The north respects such men from afar: whoever burns, burns out. Right now he charges into battle, laughing. Character: wild, joyful and reckless — fearless to the point of madness; his mouth open in a roaring laugh, his eyes wide and burning with the scarlet glow of the stone. A big northern man in his thirties with a wild red-blond beard and braids and a broad scarred face. Pose, the moment of the charge: the camera is low; he charges toward the right, his torso thrown forward. He has exactly two arms: his near hand swings a broad northern sword up and forward toward the right, and a scarlet fire stone set at the base of its blade blazes like a coal, flames running along the edge (Fire); his far arm is flung back and wide, the fist clenched. Details that tell his story: (1) fresh cuts across his arms that he does not feel; (2) a bare chest under an open fur-trimmed leather vest, a thick iron torc at his neck; (3) the glow of the stone reflected in his eyes; (4) old white scars everywhere; (5) sparks and embers swirl around him. Place: a northern battlefield at night: snow and ash, burning shields, dark pines. Scarlet light of the Fire school rises from the embers below and blazes from his blade.

jobs.subject: Subject: Seymour, chief of the north, a defender and warrior of the Fire school. Who he is: the chief of the north and the best fighter of his time, who was given a boy to raise for the throne. He taught him as everyone was taught — he went out and struck until the boy understood; the boy learned to strike fast, but not to fall. Falling takes longer to learn than striking: the one who falls must get up the same person who fell. Right now he steps onto the sand to teach his last lesson. Character: stern, proud and fatherly — a great warrior at peace with being surpassed; his face calm and fierce at once, his grey eyes steady, a faint grim smile. A huge northern man in his fifties with a grey-streaked braided beard and a scarred shaved head with a warrior's topknot. Pose, the moment of the lesson: the camera is low; he stands on the arena sand, turned toward the right, his weight forward. He has exactly two arms: his near arm raises a heavy round shield rimmed with iron toward the right and catches a blow; the rim blazes with scarlet fire where the blow lands, sparks bursting (Fire); his far hand holds a single heavy axe low and ready. Details that tell his story: (1) a thick golden chief's torc at his neck; (2) a bearskin cloak on his shoulders; (3) old pale scars across his forearms; (4) the shield is battered, with two deep axe notches in the rim; (5) sand kicked up around him. Place: the great arena of the north at dusk: sand, tall stone walls, banners, a crowd blurred in the torchlight. Scarlet light of the Fire school rises from the braziers and from cracks in the sand below.

jobs.source: roster.js c4-41: «Первый артельный старшина, которого выбрали сами скреплённые. jobs.subject: Subject: Arman the First Foreman, a man of the great harbor city, a defender of the Water school. Who he is: before him the work gangs of the harbor were ruled by overseers with a stick in one hand and a ledger in the other. One winter, on the quay by the water, the bound debtors of the harbor raised their hands — not for bread and not against the stick, but for him. He wore a bracelet of middling thickness, counted barrels faster than the clerks and never struck anyone who stood below him on the gangway. When the guards took him, the whole port stood still until they brought him back. Right now he stands between his gang and the guards. Character: calm, fair and unbudging — a man people follow; his broad face firm, his jaw set, his eyes steady and fixed on the guards beyond the right edge. A broad-shouldered man in his forties with close-cropped dark hair, a short beard and weathered skin. Pose, the moment of the stand: the camera is low; he stands on the stone quay, turned toward the right, planted like a bollard. He has exactly two arms: his near arm raises toward the right a round shield made from the iron-bound head of a barrel, and a swirl of blue water-light of the Water school runs around its rim like a wave; his far hand holds a heavy iron dock hook low. Details that tell his story: (1) on his wrist a bracelet of middling thickness: a core of blue stone set in a band of pale green stone, glowing faintly; (2) a quill pen tucked behind his ear; (3) a docker's leather jerkin, stained with salt; (4) a crowd of dock workers stands behind him in soft focus; (5) barrels and coiled ropes on the quay. Place: the harbor of a great white-stone city at dusk: the quay, the masts of ships, canals under stone arches with glowing blue stones in their keystones, terraces of white houses with red roofs climbing the hill. Blue light of the Water school rises from the water of the harbor below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Beatrice, Smith of Bracelets, a woman of the great harbor city, a controller of the Water school. Who she is: for forty years she forged the bracelets of the bound debtors at the temple of the water god — a core of blue stone that binds, set in a band of green stone in which time does not pass. She set the core right over the pulse: the spell binds not the hand but what beats in the chest. The thickness is set by the debt, not by the smith. She swept the green dust from the floor by the forge and kept it in a pouch that glows in the dark. One day the order came to forge a bracelet for her own son. Right now she binds an enemy with a ring of blue light. Character: strong, exact and hard as her craft — a master who never asks why; grief held behind a stern face; her jaw set, her eyes focused. A powerful woman in her fifties with grey-streaked hair tied back, soot on her cheek and heavy forearms. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she stands at her forge, turned toward the right. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is thrust out toward the right, and a glowing ring of blue light of the Water school flies from her fingers and closes around the enemy beyond the right edge like a bracelet; her far hand holds smith's tongs gripping a glowing bracelet fresh from the fire — a blue stone core in a pale green band. Details that tell her story: (1) a heavy leather apron scorched by forty years at the forge; (2) a small pouch at her belt glows green through the leather — the swept dust of the green stone; (3) burn scars on her forearms; (4) a thin, light bracelet of a young man's size hangs on a nail by the forge; (5) sparks and blue glints fly from the anvil. Place: the forge of the temple of the water god at night: stone arches, an anvil, a forge fire with a blue tint, the blue spires of the temple visible through a high window. Blue light of the Water school rises from the forge below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Honoré the First Bill, a man of the great harbor city, a gatherer of wealth. Who he is: when the blue stone first began to glow, he was the first to bring a bill of exchange — a paper in which one promises another — to the temple smiths and asked them to seal not the paper but the word. From then on a bill became a thing that could be neither torn nor forgotten, and within twenty years the whole world borrowed through his city. His own first bill he never repaid: the neighbour who had lent to him died, and the seal holds until the debt is paid; for forty years he carried it in his chest like the chill of well water. Right now he raises the first sealed bill. Character: shrewd, proud and quietly haunted — a clever man who made his city the creditor of the world; a thin smile, sharp eyes, a hand pressed to his chest where the chill lives. A lean man in his sixties with silver hair and a neat beard, in rich but sober clothes. Pose, the moment of the seal: the camera is low; he stands at a tall window, turned toward the right. He has exactly two arms: his near hand holds up toward the right a folded document closed with a round seal of glowing blue stone that throws blue light across his face — nothing written is visible; his far hand is pressed flat against his chest. Details that tell his story: (1) a long coat of deep blue wool with silver buttons and a merchant's chain; (2) small brass scales and a stack of coins on the table beside him; (3) a thick ledger with an iron clasp, closed, on the table; (4) a thin rime of frost on the fingers pressed to his chest; (5) through the window, ships entering the harbor far below. Place: his house on the upper tier of the great white-stone city at dusk: cypresses outside the window, the harbor full of ships below, canals under arches with glowing blue keystones. Blue light from the seal and from the canals below; warm lamplight inside.

jobs.subject: Subject: Adelaide of the Cradle, a woman of the great harbor city, a priestess and healer of the Water school. Who she is: she led the rite at the western cradle beneath Temple Hill: two people come of their own will and lay their hands on the stone, and she says the old words; when the cradle answers, the stone under their palms grows warm, as if someone turned over inside it. She held her hand over theirs and felt it first. Year by year the cradle answered less often, and she went on serving. Right now she lays her hand on the cradle, and it answers with light. Character: devoted, gentle and quietly stubborn — hope held against silence; her face serene and sad, her eyes shining. A woman in her fifties with a kind, lined face and silver-streaked hair under a white veil. Pose, the moment of healing: the camera is low; she stands beside the great cradle stone, turned toward the right. She has exactly two arms: her far hand rests on the smooth top of the cradle stone, and blue light of the Water school wells up under her palm; her near arm is stretched toward the right, the palm open, and a stream of soft blue light flows from it toward the wounded beyond the right edge. Details that tell her story: (1) priestess robes of white linen with a blue band and a white veil; (2) the cradle is a great smooth ancient stone like a basin, worn by countless hands; (3) a small silver bowl of water at her belt; (4) her hands are old and gentle; (5) the stone steps of the temple rise behind her. Place: the sanctuary of the western cradle at night at the foot of a hill: white stone arches, lamps, and far above, the blue spires of the temple. Blue light of the Water school rises from the cradle stone below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Helwig the Guarantor, a dwarf woman of the harbor quarter, a controller of the Earth school who cripples her foes. Who she is: a stranger may enter the dwarven mountain only with a deal, and the mountain makes a deal with a stranger only if one of its own vouches for him. She vouched from the harbor quarter: looked at the person, asked what he carried and how he would pay, and put her own name beside his. For thirty years she vouched for two hundred and seven people and was never wrong about them — only about their price. Right now she brings the full weight of the mountain's judgment down on an enemy. Character: shrewd, dry and immovable — a dwarf who weighs everyone; one eyebrow raised, her mouth a thin knowing line, her eyes measuring. A dwarf woman in her sixties, short and enormously broad, with thick grey braids bound with bronze rings and a broad weathered face. Pose, the moment of the judgment: the camera is low; she stands on the stone quay, turned toward the right. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is raised toward the right and slams down a heavy bronze seal, and a crushing wave of amber-orange light of the Earth school falls from it onto the enemy beyond the right edge like the weight of a mountain; her far arm holds a thick ledger bound in leather with an iron clasp, firmly closed, against her chest. Details that tell her story: (1) the ledger is closed with an iron clasp — nothing written is visible; (2) a clay jug of oil stands beside her; (3) a heavy dwarven coat of dark leather with bronze buttons; (4) small brass scales at her belt; (5) the harbor quarter behind her. Place: the harbor quarter of a great white-stone city at dusk: a quay, ships, and far away on the horizon the dark mass of the dwarven mountain. Amber light of the Earth school rises from cracks in the quay stones below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Lysander the Smuggler, a man of the great harbor city, a swift fighter of the Air school. Who he is: he slipped past the convoys in the fog off the cape in a light boat without lights; where a heavy ship waits for a mage to clear the fog, a light boat passes by ear. For nine years the convoy chased him and never caught him; he carried wine, salt and people who needed not to be written down. What caught him in the end was not a boat but a record. Right now a patrol boat looms out of the fog, and he strikes first. Character: cocky, quick and charming, fearless in the dark; a sly half-smile, bright watchful eyes. A lean man in his thirties with a stubbled jaw, dark tousled hair and a small gold earring. Pose, the moment of the strike: the camera is low; he stands in the bow of a narrow black boat, turned toward the right, leaning forward. He has exactly two arms: his near hand has just flung a long knife toward the right, and a spiral of pale white-green wind of the Air school carries it through the fog; his far hand holds a long oar upright beside him. The fog swirls open along the flight of the knife. Details that tell his story: (1) a dark oiled cloak with the hood thrown back, beaded with mist; (2) a row of throwing knives in a bandolier across his chest; (3) barrels lashed under a tarpaulin in the boat; (4) a thin bracelet with a blue stone on his wrist — the price he paid in the end; (5) a shuttered lantern at his belt, dark. Place: the fog off a rocky cape at night: dark water, the lantern of a convoy ship blurred in the fog, the glow of a lighthouse far away. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the water below; cold fog all around.

jobs.subject: Subject: Merun the Elder, a man of the first settlement, a defender and controller of the Earth school. Who he is: in the first ages, wanderers in robes taught people with their hands; one of them gave them ten words, and people repeated them at the stones. The next day one of them killed another; the wanderer heard everyone, said 'you will decide' and left, and everyone looked at him — the eldest, with no stake in it. He heard both sides again from the beginning and pronounced the first judgment in history. His name is in no book. Right now he stops a quarrel with one raised hand. Character: wise, just and unbending — an old man whose word holds a whole people; his face calm and grave, his eyes steady and deep. A tall old man with a long white beard, a weathered face and strong hands. Pose, the moment of judgment: the camera is low; he stands before the stones, turned toward the right. He has exactly two arms: his near arm is raised toward the right with the palm open — stop — and a wall of amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the ground in front of him, holding back the one beyond the right edge; his far hand grips a tall staff of rough wood planted in the earth. Details that tell his story: (1) a simple robe of rough undyed wool with a rope belt; (2) the big calloused hands of a builder; (3) ten plain, uncarved standing stones stand in a row behind him — no marks on them; (4) a small bronze knife and a pouch at his belt; (5) the huts of the first settlement around the stones. Place: the first settlement at dawn: ten plain standing stones, low huts of wood and clay, a young world of open hills. Amber light rises from the earth below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Sabina of the Circle, a woman of the great harbor city, a healer of the Light school who also cripples her foes. Who she is: a midwife at the western cradle who saw more couples than the priests, and by her fortieth year the cradle was silent more often than not. The priests taught that the circle is whole and the fault lies with the parents; she knew it was not so, and said it — first in a whisper, then aloud on the square by the fountain. She healed with a light that none of the five schools gives, and took no payment for it. Right now she heals with that light on the square. Character: brave, warm and defiant — she wants only to be heard; her chin raised, her mouth open as she speaks aloud, her eyes shining. A woman in her forties with a strong, kind face and dark hair, a simple grey hood pushed back. Pose, the moment of the light: the camera is low; she stands by a fountain, turned toward the right. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is raised toward the right, and a warm stream of pale golden light of the Light school pours from her palm toward the sick beyond the right edge; her far hand is pressed to her heart. Details that tell her story: (1) a plain grey robe with a hood, the sleeves rolled up over a midwife's arms; (2) no purse at her belt — she takes no payment; (3) a copper basin and linen cloths beside her; (4) a small bundle of dried herbs; (5) guards with halberds watch the square in soft focus. Place: a square with a fountain in the great white-stone city at dusk: arches, water, and the blue spires of the temple on the hill above. Pale golden light of the Light school rises from the water of the fountain below.
